title: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1 - Ethics & Professional Responsibilities - Handling Cash - Limits
exam: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1
subject: Ethics & Professional Responsibilities

questions.q: A client approaches a paralegal to handle a series of complex Provincial Offences Act (POA) matters. The client offers to pay an $8,500 advance retainer in cash. Under the Law Society of Ontario (LSO) By-laws, what is the paralegal's obligation?
options: Accept the cash, deposit it into the mixed trust account, and issue a receipt.
Decline the cash payment, as paralegals cannot accept more than $7,500 in cash in respect of any one client matter, subject to limited exceptions.
Accept the cash but notify the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC).
Accept the cash but divide it into two separate trust deposits to avoid the cash limit rule.
questions.explain: Under LSO By-law 9, a legal practitioner is prohibited from receiving or accepting cash in an aggregate amount of $7,500 or more in Canadian dollars in respect of any one client matter, to prevent money laundering. Splitting deposits to evade this is also strictly prohibited.
